detail.title: Compositional Heredity across Growth-Division Regimes
detail.summary: Multistable autocatalytic reaction networks exhibit compositional memory, allowing stable states to be maintained across growth-division cycles. This memory is driven by the feedback between chemical kinetics and compartment growth, where stochastic transitions between states act as primitive mutations.
detail.reason: Notebook revision required by governance to integrate recent evidence regarding thermodynamic drivers of natural selection in prebiotic networks.

detail.title: Fidelity Thresholds for Prebiotic Evolution
detail.summary: Minimal copying fidelity is essential for open-ended evolution in templated systems to avoid error catastrophe. However, non-templated autocatalytic networks may maintain compositional heredity through bistable reaction subgraphs, potentially circumventing traditional error thresholds found in linear replicators. Stoichiometric conditions on these networks provide formal criteria for sustaining stable heritable states.
detail.reason: Revision required to synthesize evidence on stoichiometric conditions and thermodynamic limits, advancing the project beyond initial conceptualization.
